title: Sunday's datebook
text:
SUPPORT GROUPS
The Caring Place has a support group for primary caregivers of individuals with Alzheimer's and dementia/dementia-related illnesses on the fourth Wednesday of each month. The meeting is held at the Oaklawn Center on Aging, 307-F Carpenter Dam Road, from 11:30 a.m. to 1 p.m. Lunch is provided. Care will be provided for loved ones during the meeting and lunch for those who need it. For more information, call The Caring Place at 501-623-2881.
Narcotics Anonymous meets at noon Monday through Saturday and at 2 p.m. Sundays at 315 W. Grand Ave. This is a 12-step recovery program for people for whom drugs have become a major problem. The Helpline number is 501-321-8700.
Alcoholics Anonymous meets daily at 8 p.m.; at 8 a.m. Monday, Wednesday and Friday; at noon Monday-Saturday; and at 6:30 p.m. Sunday. The speaker meeting is at 11 a.m. Sunday. The step meeting is at 6 p.m. Tuesday. The men's and women's meeting is at 6 p.m. Friday. All meetings are held at 411 Sellers St. Call 501-623-6328 for more information.
Alcoholics Anonymous, Last House on the Block, meets at 6 and 8 a.m. today at 315 W. Grand Ave. Call 866-754-2579.
Alcoholics Anonymous, Malvern Group, meets at 8 p.m. today at 211 W. Third St., in Malvern, in the upstairs Chamber of Commerce Building. Doors open at 7 p.m. Call 501-467-5409 or 501-231-9518 for AA information, or 501-623-6328 for Hot Springs Intergroup.
Al-Anon, 1806 Central Ave., First Christian Church, meets Monday and Thursday at 11 a.m. Call Melinda at 501-520-7876 for more information.
National Alliance for Mental Illness will meet at 12:30 p.m. Monday at Garland County Library, Meeting Room B. NAMI is a support group for those with loved ones with mental health issues. For information, text 501-655-1747 or 501-538-6999.
Adult Children of Alcoholics and Dysfunctional Families (ACDA) meets at 6 p.m. Tuesdays and Thursdays at St. Luke's Episcopal Church, 228 Spring St. ACA is a 12-step program that focuses on emotional sobriety. The members are affected by the dysfunction in their families of origin, whether alcohol was present in the home or not. For more information, call Jodie at 501-538-2046.
MISCELLANEOUS
Hot Springs AIDS Clinic, 1801 Central Ave., Suite C, is open from 9 a.m.-4 p.m. Monday-Friday. The clinic provides free, comprehensive medical care, lab testing, medications, case management and support groups. Call Mike Melancon at 501-623-5598 for more information.
Cans for Kids donates canned and boxed food items and helps provide meals to children in all nine Garland County schools. Call 501-321-2517 for information.
Teen Clinic provides optional STD testing, pregnancy prevention and medical exams in partnership with Garland County Health Department, family planning and clinic services. Call Melissa Draper, outreach and volunteer coordinator, 501-623-5591, ext. 10, or email [[email protected]](/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection).
Veterans Transportation Network needs volunteer drivers to take veterans to appointments. To volunteer, call 501-257-6991 or 501-257-3288.
The Literacy Council of the Ouachitas offers free, confidential tutoring for adults in reading, basic math and computer literacy. English as a Second Language and citizenship tutoring are also available. Adult tutors are needed on an ongoing basis. Call 501-624-7323, email Sarah Richardson at [[email protected]](/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection), or visit http://OuachitaLiteracy.org for more information.
American Legion Post No. 13 welcomes new members and supporters and meets at the post home, 3237 Albert Pike, Hot Springs, the first Sunday of each month at 3 p.m. The Sons of the Legion meets at 1:30 p.m. The 40-8 Lounge is open daily and has Happy Hour from 5-6 p.m. For more information, call 501-767-1346.
